pairs.subject: eval-harness
pairs.evidence: crates/engine/src/judge.rs:367 Mixed rubrics invoke model judgment even after a deterministic dimension breaches its gating floor, violating the requirement that assertions screen out failed outputs before judgment.

techniques.evidence: crates/engine/src/judge.rs:367 Model sampling depends on dimension kinds rather than deterministic gate success; the deterministic-floor test also supplies and consumes an LLM style verdict for the mechanically wrong answer.
crates/engine/src/pairwise.rs:66 The pairwise path judges both presentation orders, reverses the second verdict's labels, and converts disagreement into a tie with a position-bias flag.

pairs.subject: eval-harness
pairs.evidence: crates/runner/src/pairwise.rs:422 The pairwise runner sorts every candidate into a win-rate ranking without checking completed-comparison connectivity or enforcing an exposure floor.

techniques.evidence: crates/runner/src/pairwise.rs:530 The pairwise report is explicitly identified as pairwise and records no_baseline rather than presenting relative preference as an absolute passing gate.

crates/runner/src/stats/effort_curve.rs:223 The effort-step cost delta includes all shared judged cases without filtering both arms' pass fields, and its report has no both-succeeded companion delta or subset count.

crates/runner/src/pairwise.rs:422 print_ranking sorts all labels by completed-game win rate without a connectivity check or minimum completed exposure; a planned round-robin does not guarantee the completed graph remains connected.

crates/runner/src/pairwise.rs:326 Exclusions are charged to both participants and positional ties are disclosed, but ranking still includes candidates with arbitrarily large excluded shares, including candidates that played no games.

pairs.subject: eval-harness
pairs.evidence: crates/api/src/benchmarks.rs:70 Benchmark creation defaults to a capability alias rather than a concrete dated judge identifier, allowing the instrument to change while the stored judge specification remains unchanged.

techniques.evidence: crates/api/src/benchmarks.rs:70 The API's default judge is an alias plus effort, not the concrete dated model pin required by the standard.

crates/api/src/prompts_gate.rs:107 After the trust check, force=true allows promotion before regression and incomplete-evidence checks, so a declared quality constraint can be overridden after the result is known.

pairs.subject: eval-harness
pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/score.rs:462 Deserializing a benchmark without a judge_model selects a moving alias rather than a concrete dated judge, weakening the identity of the measurement instrument.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/score.rs:462 Benchmark's serde default supplies haiku, a capability alias; a missing judge specification therefore does not obtain a concrete dated pin.

pairs.subject: eval-harness
pairs.evidence: crates/render/src/benchmarks.rs:61 The run-history renderer combines all available means into one trend without separating instrument versions, allowing methodology changes to appear as changes in product quality.

techniques.evidence: crates/render/src/benchmarks.rs:61 runs collects every non-null mean and renders a single sparkline; it neither checks instrument pins nor partitions or marks the trend when they change.
